questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The culture in South Korea. As a landscape architect student/designer, Japan and South Korea are constantly mentioned as places to visit. I wanted to experience this first hand and see what inspirations Incan take back with me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I would give it a 10, the only problem, was the language barrier was much harder than I thought. This side of the world, English is not that common at all, so be prepared to learn a lot of the language before travelling there.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was hard to find information upon arrival. The process of selecting a course related to your studies and being accepted was hard and confusing.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was an office in which helped out students with courses.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was quite easy to find housing off campus in my case. This depends on how much money you are willing to pay of course also. YouTube is the best place to indulge in to get all knowledge on what sorts of websites to use etc. Shared apartments are common, also if you need a quick place to settle and for cheap, there are goshiwon's which has shower and toilet inside. It's very small so bare that in mind when looking for this.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: In Seoul, it's a big city so living off campus may be far to get to university. But in my opinion, experience the city first, experience the culture, don't worry about living 40 minutes away on a train from campus, because you'll still be in the city and a great way to explore more. I think you should enjoy taking in the city vibe when going abroad for study.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: This was hard to find courses and get accepted onto courses. Even if you followed the instructions, it wasn't so simple. I was disappointed with this actually.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The only help was the help desk at the international office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Unsuccessful. I had to take a course that wasn't so related to mine. However, this was not a huge problem for me as you gain more knowledge in other subject areas.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Arrive on campus before course starts and go to the help desk to let them help you choose the courses you desire. Go well before the courses start.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses are similar to your home university. Students take education seriously and work hard.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar, no difference.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Read the World of Film Through Feminism.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Choose courses which genuinely interest you, this is almost a once in a life time opportunity to do it.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: The price of buying a SIM with internet is cheap. Also, certain times in the supermarket to buy food is expensive. However, it is quite cheap in Seoul.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything in general was less expensive than I thought.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Football, art clubs, many clubs are available here.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Art club.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Visit historical and cultural sites, go to the mountain and see things in general. Definitely take in the cafe culture, it is very nice here.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy, people don't really make you feel uncomfortable, you sit right in. Also Korean people are very friendly.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just ask questions, they are always open to try help any way they can. Don't be afraid to do things on your own, its apart of growth here.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Language barrier was really hard.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Cafe culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- Go out and explore
- Arrive in Seoul well in advance before your school starts and sort out your courses.
- Don't be afraid to do things by yourself.
- Lastly, don't follow huge crowds, be smart and don't get in the middle of large crowds.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talk to people, no one ignores you.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning to be able to be by myself when you're the only one available. Also, being able to manage my money better and going out habits. I feel as though I have matured a lot.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Managing my money.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
